newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani Gulf war victims get UN compensation.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani Gulf war victims get UN compensation.

text.p: The United Nations Compensation Commission (UNCC) has awarded $150 million to Pakistanis affected by the 1991 Gulf War, an official of Overseas Pakistani's Foundation (OPF) said on Monday.

He said $10 million had been paid by UNCC to the OPF for 4,126 claims approved so far against a total of 44,000 claims made by people disturbed and injured and relatives of people who died in the war that followed the Iraqi invasion of Kuwait in 1990.

"I am happy that with the help of UNCC, the affectees have been compensated and an amount of $10.292 million is being disbursed," Pakistani Interior Minister Chaudhry Shujaat Hussain said at a cheque-distribution ceremony.
"The rest of the affectees will also, hopefully, be compensated soon after finalisation of their cases," he said.
Manzoor Ahmed, 50, who was a tailor in Kuwait at the time of the war, told Reuters the UNCC had approved his claim of $4,000 but he had received a cheque only for an equivalent amount of $2,500.
"If I had received the full amount today, I could have used it to buy a piece of land to make a small house," Ahmed said. "Now this might just get spent by me," he added.
OPF assistant director for Kuwait Celll, Bilar Tahir, said every claimant was being paid $2,500 as the first installment under UNCC guidelines.
